minutes.headline: Commission approved five wetlands permits, set FY27 fund budgets, and resolved a driveway wetlands violation without a fine
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission acted on a full slate of wetlands hearings — approving several driveway, septic and carport projects, continuing others pending planning-board or DEP action — and resolved an unpermitted driveway culvert at 314 Highland Street with remediation (riprap and on-site wetland replication) rather than a fine. The commission also set FY2027 budgets for its Hollis Road, Timber Rights and Wetlands Bylaw Fees accounts, while flagging unresolved confusion over the Mass Trails grant account balance, ARPA matching funds, and a town-manager-held bequest fund with no visibility to the commission.

budget_items.what_was_said: The commission noted the town no longer has a dedicated social media manager after the new budget. Office staff have reportedly been trained to handle social media instead, including for the invasives event.
Commissioners asked for an update on where the Mass Trails grant budget stands, since the volunteer tracking it and town finance had not reported back. No figures were given at this point.
The agent reported the revised fund balance on the year-to-date report appears negative, raising questions about how drawdowns and reimbursements are being recorded.

budget_items.topic: Proposed fine for 314 Highland Street violation
budget_items.what_was_said: The agent floated a possible fine for the unpermitted culvert and driveway work, but most commissioners favored remediation only given it appeared an honest mistake.
A bequest fund held for the commission is tracked by the town manager directly through a bank rather than through MUNIS, so the commission has no visibility into its balance or usage rules.

budget_items.topic: Hollis Road revolving fund FY27 balance
budget_items.what_was_said: The agent presented the prior fund balance, this year's changes, and the current balance to use as the basis for next year's Hollis Road budget.

budget_items.topic: Hollis Road purchase-of-service line, prior year
budget_items.what_was_said: Last year's purchase-of-service sub-account was set at one figure with a chunk left unspent, prompting discussion of whether to keep that split given custodian income has stopped.
The agent proposed putting a fixed amount into purchase of service and the remainder into maintenance of grounds, noting the full balance would be available since custodian income had stopped.
The commission voted to set the Hollis Road sub-account budgets for fiscal year 2027 at the proposed figures.

budget_items.topic: Timber Rights fund, prior year split
budget_items.what_was_said: Last year's Timber Rights budget put a small amount to purchase of service and the rest to supplies, out of a fund with roughly this total balance.
A town official confirmed that anything over a stated dollar threshold in services must go out to bid with prevailing wages, which caps how much can go to the purchase-of-service line.

budget_items.topic: Matching funds for Table Rock/Reno trail grants
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners discussed needing matching funds, likely from Timber Rights, if pending grant applications for parking area work at Table Rock and Reno are awarded.
The commission voted to set the FY2027 Timber Rights sub-account budgets between purchase of service and supplies at the proposed figures.
The agent reported the fund's current balance from permitting fees and recommended budgeting about half of it for now, pending a planned guided-hike program and flyers.

budget_items.topic: Wetlands Bylaw Fees FY27 budget vote
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission voted to set the Wetlands Protection Bylaw Fees fund budget at the proposed figure to cover items like flyers and guided-hike materials.

budget_items.topic: Mass Trails grant spending to date
budget_items.what_was_said: The year-to-date report showed spending against the grant's budgeted amount, plus an unexplained encumbrance that commissioners could not immediately identify.
Commissioners tried to reconcile the encumbrance against the total grant request and the matching-fund percentage the commission had committed to.

budget_items.topic: Mass Trails/DCR reimbursement and ARPA match
budget_items.what_was_said: Reading from an old email, commissioners noted a partial reimbursement received from the state and a separate ARPA-funded matching amount the town had allocated.

Only a small amount of ARPA funding was left showing against the grant when the town's ARPA spending deadline passed, and it is unclear whether obligations already contracted for were properly covered before those funds expired.

decisions.decision: Minutes from the June 3, 2026 meeting were tabled to the next meeting because a quorum of members who attended that meeting was not present to vote.
This year's invasive-plant removal effort will use manual removal only, since no one is currently licensed to apply herbicide on public land.
Agreed to arrange a meeting among the agent, the chair, the town's grant volunteer and the finance/grants staffer to sort out the Mass Trails grant account before the fiscal year closes.
Commissioners agreed informally to pursue riprap fill in the culvert plus an on-site wetland replication area at 314 Highland Street rather than requiring removal of the pipe or imposing a fine.
Commission will revisit updating the wetlands bylaw and permitting fee structure once the agent meets with town legal counsel about the process.
Agreed to set up a meeting between the town manager, the chair, and possibly a commissioner regarding a new custodial agreement for the Hollis Road property.
Commission will consider adding a recurring 'commissioner updates' or property-updates subsection to future agendas.
Agent will informally raise with the Select Board the idea of an Eagle Scout project to re-seed and plant natives at the town-owned Zero Reservoir Road parcel where a past encroachment was cleared.

what_happened.line: Commission approved remediation (riprap and wetland replication) rather than a fine for an unpermitted driveway culvert at 314 Highland Street.

Commission approved wetlands permits for projects including a common driveway with a drainage basin, a demolition/reconstruction, and a failed septic system replacement, while continuing several others to July for planning-board or state review.
Commission voted to set FY2027 budgets for the Hollis Road, Timber Rights, and Wetlands Protection Bylaw Fees funds.
Commission flagged an apparently negative Mass Trails grant fund balance and a commission-held bequest fund tracked by the town manager outside normal accounting, with no resolution reached.

why_it_matters: Resolving a wetlands violation with remediation instead of a fine sets a visible precedent for how the town handles unpermitted work discovered near wetlands.
The permit votes clear or delay specific driveway, septic and construction projects for the property owners involved.
The Mass Trails grant and bequest-fund questions concern how public conservation money is tracked, which the commission says it currently cannot fully see.
